gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Minn Kota QUEST motors can draw up to 60 A on high speed, so a lithium battery has to hold at least 60 A continuously. Redodo's own 36V 50Ah (sold for 100–120 lb motors) is rated 50 A continuous and 60 A only for up to 30 minutes, and its 24V 50Ah is rated 60 A only for 30 minutes. Its 24V 100Ah has a 100 A BMS and clears 60 A with room to spare.
standout_why: ChatGPT cited three Minn Kota pages: the Wiring & Battery Guide (its body did not load for me), 'Trolling Motor Power Considerations' and 'Deep Cycle Battery Selection'. The second and third give only the general rule that a lithium battery's continuous discharge must cover the motor's max amp draw, plus the advice to stay at speed 8.5 or below on brushed motors. Neither gives the 60 A QUEST ceiling or ties the rule to a battery's BMS rating. The 'Lithium Battery Selection' page was in the results but not cited. It adds that Minn Kota's onboard PCL chargers top out at 14.5 V, but it also gives no QUEST amp figure. The 60 A figure is only on two Minn Kota help pages ChatGPT did not get: 'Troubleshooting Power' and 'Amp Draw, Circuit Breakers, Fuses'. Rivals have the rule but not the number or the pairing, so I scored 2 rather than 3. The number is what rules out the 50Ah Redodo boxes for QUEST motors.
kit_items: Battery: Redodo 24V 100Ah LiFePO4 (100 A BMS, 2,560 Wh, $469.99). It covers the 60 A a 24V Minn Kota QUEST motor can pull, which Redodo's 24V 50Ah (60 A for only 30 minutes) does not. One 24V battery replaces the two 12V batteries in series.

Charger: Redodo 29.2V 20A MINI LiFePO4 charger ($109.99). Redodo says it is built for 24V LiFePO4 and fully charges a 24V 100Ah in about 5 hours, the same charger and time the battery listing names. A 24V lead-acid charger or a Minn Kota onboard charger set for lead-acid is not the matched choice; Minn Kota says to check the charge profile with the battery maker.
